claims.text: The proposed method targets multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
The methodological intervention is to develop machine-learning-based interatomic potentials.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can provide an improved interatomic-potential reference for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials will better represent the atomic configurations sampled by an ab initio liquid.
Better representation of ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The machine-learning reference will produce less thermodynamic-integration path mismatch than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Reduced path mismatch will improve predictions of thermodynamic properties such as free energy.
The intervention is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy-alloy compositions and temperatures relevant to high-temperature applications.
Molecular-dynamics results from machine-learning potentials can be compared against EAM results and experimental or first-principles data.
Free energy and thermodynamic-integration path mismatch are the proposed experimental measurements.
Failure to improve liquid-configuration representation or to produce a significant reduction in path mismatch would falsify the hypothesis.
